passage: Mr Arnab, the maths teacher, had taught Gopika for two years, and she was usually first with her hand up. Today her eyelids were heavy and half closed, her head propped on her palm. When he asked a question she took a while to look up. A few classmates smirked. Arnab felt a flash of irritation and thought, is she being rude? He held it back. After the bell he said, "Gopika, you seem very tired today. How has your sleep been?" She rubbed her red eyes. "I was on my phone till two, sir, finishing a project video. Sorry." He nodded. "Thank you for telling me. Let us talk about how to space it out."

qa.q: What was Gopika's head propped on?
qa.a: Gopika's head was propped on her palm.

qa.q: What did Arnab think when he first saw Gopika's half-closed eyes?
qa.a: He felt irritation and wondered if she was being rude, but held it back. He then chose to ask about sleep, since tiredness was another likely reason.

qa.q: What did Arnab do that avoided assuming disrespect?
qa.a: He asked how her sleep had been, listened to her answer and offered to talk about spacing the work out.

qa.q: How might Gopika have felt when the classmates smirked?
qa.a: She was probably embarrassed and too tired to respond, and may have worried she looked disrespectful.

grounding: A teenager with half-closed eyes after late screen time may look rude but is simply tired, and an adult asks about sleep first.

passage:
Last year, I spent many nights watching videos on my phone until two in the morning. I didn't realise how tired I looked the next day.
In Irawati Ma'am's science class, my eyelids felt so heavy I kept rubbing my eyes. My head drooped. I heard someone whisper, "She's bored again."
Ma'am came over. I expected her to scold me. Instead she said quietly, "Simran, did you sleep last night?"
I shook my head. "Not much."
She nodded. "It shows. After class, let's talk about a sleep plan."
We talked for ten minutes. She didn't tell me off. She just asked me to try putting the phone outside the room for one week. It actually helped.
- Simran

qa.q: How late did Simran stay up watching videos?
qa.a: Until two in the morning.

qa.q: What was Simran feeling when Ma'am came over?
qa.a: Simran felt worried and expected to be scolded for looking bored.

qa.q: What did Irawati Ma'am do that was wise?
qa.a: She asked about sleep before assuming Simran was being rude or bored.

qa.q: How might the classmate who whispered "She's bored again" see Simran differently now?
qa.a: That classmate might realise Simran was tired, not bored, and that tiredness can look like disinterest.

grounding: The narrator recalls looking bored in class after late screen time, and a teacher asking about sleep instead of assuming disrespect.

passage:
Teacher's note, Tuesday
In English today, Santosh's eyes were half-closed, and he kept yawning. His head rested on his hand.
Some might think he was bored or disrespectful. But he's usually alert and asks questions.
After class I asked, "Santosh, did you sleep well?"
He admitted he'd been playing games online till late. "I didn't mean to be rude, Ma'am."
I told him I didn't think he was rude, just tired. We agreed he'd try to switch off his phone by ten, and he'd tell me if he felt too tired to focus.
I'll check in with him on Friday.
- Ms Elizabeth

qa.q: What did Santosh say he'd been doing late at night?
qa.a: Playing games online till late.

qa.q: What was Santosh feeling when he said "I didn't mean to be rude"?
qa.a: He felt worried and guilty that his tiredness looked like disrespect.

qa.q: What did Ms Elizabeth do that helped?
qa.a: She asked about sleep instead of assuming rudeness and made a simple plan with Santosh.

qa.q: How might the class have seen Santosh's heavy eyes?
qa.a: Some classmates might think he was bored or rude, not realising he was simply tired.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a teenager looking bored due to late screen time, and the teacher asking about sleep.

passage:
Wednesday
Mohit Sir asked me in class, "Am I boring you, Gopika?" Everyone laughed. My face went hot.
I wasn't bored. I was chatting with Neha till one in the morning about the school fest, and then I scrolled through fest photos in the dark. My eyes felt sandy all day and kept closing by themselves, even in the maths period, which I actually like.
After class, Sir called me aside. "Are you getting enough sleep?"
I said, "Not really, Sir."
He said, "Okay. It looked like boredom, but I shouldn't have assumed. Try to rest tonight."
I felt better. I'm going to leave my phone in the kitchen tonight.
- Gopika

qa.q: Who was Gopika chatting with until one in the morning?
qa.a: Neha.

qa.q: What was Gopika feeling when the class laughed?
qa.a: Gopika felt embarrassed and hot-faced, since the tiredness was mistaken for boredom.

qa.q: What did Mohit Sir do after class that helped?
qa.a: He asked about sleep, admitted he shouldn't have assumed, and encouraged rest.

qa.q: How might Mohit Sir have felt after learning Gopika was just tired?
qa.a: He may have felt a bit sorry for assuming Gopika was bored and glad he asked.

grounding: A teenager's diary shows tiredness from late-night chatting being mistaken for boredom, and a teacher then asking about sleep.
